extracted.intended_audience: investment advisers registered or required to be registered under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940; compliance officers and supervised persons
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory compliance requirements for delivery of Form ADV brochures and supplements, Form CRS, Form PF, codes of ethics, performance computation, and exemptions under Part 275 of the Advisers Act. Includes filing, delivery timing, exemptions, recordkeeping, reporting, and definitional rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to deliver brochure and brochure supplements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are registered under the Act as an investment adviser, you must deliver a brochure and one or more brochure supplements to each client or prospective client that contains all information required by Part 2 of Form ADV [17 CFR 279.1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to each client or prospective client; brochures and supplements must include all information required by Part 2/Part 2B of Form ADV. See delivery timing and exceptions in subsequent provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver current brochure at or before contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to a client or prospective client your current brochure before or at the time you enter into an investment advisory contract with that client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be the most recent revision (current brochure). Delivery may be performed by you or a supervised person acting on your behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual delivery / summary of material changes within 120 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client, annually within 120 days after the end of your fiscal year and without charge, if there are material changes in your brochure since your last annual updating amendment: (i) a current brochure, or (ii) the summary of material changes to the brochure as required by Item 2 of Form ADV, Part 2A that offers to provide your current brochure without charge, accompanied by the Web site address (if available) and an e-mail address (if available) and telephone number by which a client may obtain the current brochure from you, and the Web site address for obtaining information about you through the Investment Adviser Public Disclosure (IAPD) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using the summary-of-material-changes option, you must offer to provide the full brochure without charge and include contact information and IAPD web address. The annual delivery requirement triggers only if material changes occurred since last annual updating amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of brochure supplements timing and team exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client or prospective client a current brochure supplement for a supervised person before or at the time that supervised person begins to provide advisory services to the client; if advice is provided by a team of more than five supervised persons, a current brochure supplement need only be delivered for the five supervised persons with the most significant responsibility for the day-to-day advice provided to that client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supervised person provides advisory services if they (i) formulate investment advice for the client and have direct client contact, or (ii) make discretionary investment decisions for the client even without direct client contact. Delivery may be by you or a supervised person acting on your behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt delivery after amended disciplinary disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client promptly after you create an amended brochure or brochure supplement, if the amendment adds disclosure of an event, or materially revises information already disclosed about an event, in response to Item 9 of Part 2A or Item 3 of Part 2B (Disciplinary Information): (i) the amended brochure or brochure supplement along with a statement describing the material facts relating to the change in disciplinary information, or (ii) a statement describing the material facts relating to the change in disciplinary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies specifically to changes in disciplinary information (Items noted). Delivery must be prompt after creation of the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to brochure delivery for certain clients
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not required to deliver a brochure to a client: (i) that is an investment company registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940 or a business development company provided the advisory contract meets section 15(c) requirements; or (ii) who receives only impersonal investment advice for which you charge less than $500 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception for registered investment companies requires the advisory contract to meet section 15(c) of the Investment Company Act. 'Impersonal investment advice' is further defined elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to brochure supplement delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not required to deliver a brochure supplement to a client: (i) to whom you are not required to deliver a brochure under the exceptions, (ii) who receives only impersonal investment advice, or (iii) who is an officer, employee, or other person related to the adviser that would be a ‘qualified client’ of your firm under § 275.205-3(d)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brochure supplement delivery exceptions mirror the brochure exceptions and add the qualified-client-related-person exception. See qualified client definition in §275.205-3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap fee program brochure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a sponsor of a wrap fee program, then the brochure that paragraph (b) requires you to deliver to a client or prospective client of the wrap fee program must be a wrap fee program brochure containing all the information required by Part 2A, Appendix 1 of Form ADV. Any additional information in a wrap fee program brochure must be limited to information applicable to wrap fee programs that you sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another program sponsor delivers a compliant wrap fee brochure to the client/prospective client, you need not deliver another. Note: a wrap fee program brochure does not replace brochure supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple brochures allowed when services differ
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide substantially different advisory services to different clients, you may provide them with different brochures, so long as each client receives all information about the services and fees that are applicable to that client. The brochure you deliver to a client may omit any information required by Part 2A of Form ADV if the information does not apply to the advisory services or fees that you will provide or charge, or that you propose to provide or charge, to that client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows tailoring brochures to client-specific services/fees but requires full disclosure of information that is applicable to that client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brochure delivery does not relieve other disclosure obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering a brochure or brochure supplement in compliance with this section does not relieve you of any other disclosure obligations you have to your advisory clients or prospective clients under any federal or state laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with these delivery rules is necessary but not sufficient to satisfy all legal disclosure obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Impersonal investment advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Impersonal investment advice means investment advisory services that do not purport to meet the objectives or needs of specific individuals or accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine exceptions to brochure and supplement delivery; the fee threshold (< $500/year) for impersonal advice is referenced in exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Current brochure/current brochure supplement
rubrics_metrics.description: Current brochure and current brochure supplement mean the most recent revision of the brochure or brochure supplement, including all amendments to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Current’ status governs what must be delivered under timing requirements (e.g., before contract, annually, upon amendment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Sponsor of a wrap fee program
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor of a wrap fee program means an investment adviser that is compensated under a wrap fee program for sponsoring, organizing, or administering the program, or for selecting, or providing advice to clients regarding the selection of, other investment advisers in the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who must prepare/ deliver wrap fee program brochures and who may rely on another sponsor's delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Supervised person
rubrics_metrics.description: Supervised person means any of your officers, partners or directors (or other persons occupying a similar status or performing similar functions) or employees, or any other person who provides investment advice on your behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term used throughout delivery and code-of-ethics rules to identify who requires disclosures, supplements, reporting obligations, and who is an access person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Wrap fee program
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrap fee program means an advisory program under which a specified fee or fees not based directly upon transactions in a client's account is charged for investment advisory services (which may include portfolio management or advice concerning the selection of other investment advisers) and the execution of client transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the program type subject to specific brochure format and content (Part 2A, Appendix 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt reporting advisers must file Form ADV
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an investment adviser relying on the exemption from registering with the Commission under section 203(l) or (m) of the Act, you must complete and file reports on Form ADV by following the instructions in the Form, which specify the information that an exempt reporting adviser must provide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exempt reporting advisers do not register but still must file Form ADV reports in accordance with Form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for Form ADV (exempt advisers)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file Form ADV electronically with the Investment Adviser Registration Depository (IARD) unless you have received a hardship exemption under paragraph (e) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on how to file with the IARD is available on the Commission's website. Hardship exemptions are available under specified procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV considered filed upon IARD acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Form ADV is considered filed with the Commission upon acceptance by the IARD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance by IARD is the operative event that constitutes filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees for Form ADV (exempt advisers)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must pay FINRA (the operator of the IARD) a filing fee. The Commission has approved the amount of the filing fee. No portion of the filing fee is refundable. Your completed Form ADV will not be accepted by FINRA, and thus will not be considered filed with the Commission, until you have paid the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is required before acceptance; fees are non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary hardship exemption for electronic filing (Form ADV)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have unanticipated technical difficulties that prevent submission of a filing to the IARD, you may request a temporary hardship exemption from the requirements of this chapter to file electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request the exemption you must file Form ADV-H in paper no later than one business day after the filing was due, and submit the filing electronically with the IARD no later than seven business days after the filing was due. The exemption is granted upon filing a completed Form ADV-H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final report filing requirements (Form ADV)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file a final report in accordance with instructions in Form ADV when: (1) you cease operation as an investment adviser; (2) you no longer meet the definition of exempt reporting adviser; or (3) you apply for registration with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You do not have to pay a filing fee to file a final report on Form ADV through the IARD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to deliver Form CRS to retail investors
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are registered under the Act as an investment adviser, you must deliver Form CRS, required by Part 3 of Form ADV, to each retail investor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form CRS delivery obligations are specific to retail investors as defined in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for delivering current Form CRS at account initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each retail investor your current Form CRS before or at the time you enter into an investment advisory contract with that retail investor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Current Form CRS’ means the most recent version; delivery may be performed by a supervised person acting on your behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for delivering updated Form CRS to existing clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each retail investor who is an existing client your current Form CRS before or at the time you: (i) open a new account that is different from the retail investor's existing account(s); (ii) recommend that the retail investor roll over assets from a retirement account into a new or existing account or investment; or (iii) recommend or provide a new investment advisory service or investment that does not necessarily involve the opening of a new account and would not be held in an existing account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are event-driven delivery obligations for existing retail clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post Form CRS prominently on website
rubrics_metrics.description: Post the current Form CRS prominently on your website, if you have one, in a location and format that is easily accessible for retail investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility and prominence are required so retail investors can readily find CRS information online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate changes to Form CRS within 60 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate any changes made to Form CRS to each retail investor who is an existing client within 60 days after the amendments are required to be made and without charge. The communication can be made by delivering the amended Form CRS or by communicating the information through another disclosure that is delivered to the retail investor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to amendments that are required to be made; communications must be timely (within 60 days) and free of charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver Form CRS upon request within 30 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver a current Form CRS to each retail investor within 30 days upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to written or other requests by retail investors for the current CRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form CRS delivery does not replace other obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivering Form CRS in compliance with this section does not relieve you of any other disclosure obligations you have to your retail investors under any Federal or State laws or regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form CRS is in addition to, not a substitute for, other legal disclosure duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to Form CRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Form CRS means the most recent version; retail investor means a natural person (or the legal representative) who seeks or receives services primarily for personal, family or household purposes; supervised person is defined as in other sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions determine who is a retail investor and who receives CRS; they affect who must be given the Form and when.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rule for Form CRS delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 30 days after the date by which you are first required to electronically file your Form CRS with the Commission, you must deliver to each of your existing clients who is a retail investor your current Form CRS as required by Part 3 of Form ADV. As of the date by which you are first required to electronically file your Form CRS with the Commission, you must begin using your Form CRS as required by Part 3 of Form ADV to comply with the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a short transition window for existing clients when Form CRS filing obligations begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PF filing obligation for advisers to private funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an investment adviser registered or required to be registered under section 203 of the Act, you act as an investment adviser to one or more private funds and, as of the end of your most recently completed fiscal year, you managed private fund assets of at least $150 million, you must complete and file a report on Form PF by following the instructions in the Form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial report due no later than the last day on which your next update would be timely if you had previously filed Form PF. No filing required for fiscal periods ending prior to registration effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing for Form PF
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file Form PF electronically with the Form PF filing system on the Investment Adviser Registration Depository (IARD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructions and filing mechanics are provided by the IARD/Form PF filing system; see SEC/IARD resources for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form PF considered filed upon acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Form PF is considered filed with the Commission upon acceptance by the Form PF filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance by the filing system constitutes filing; similar to Form ADV treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees for Form PF
rubrics_metrics.description: You must pay the operator of the Form PF filing system a filing fee as required by the instructions to Form PF. The Commission has approved the amount of the filing fee. No portion of the filing fee is refundable. Your completed Form PF will not be accepted by the operator of the Form PF filing system, and thus will not be considered filed with the Commission, until you have paid the filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee payment is required before acceptance; fees are non-refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updates to Form PF (frequency and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file an updated Form PF: (1) at least annually, no later than the date specified in the instructions to Form PF; and (2) more frequently, if required by the instructions to Form PF. You must file all updated reports electronically with the Form PF filing system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must track instruction-driven deadlines for periodic and event-driven updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary hardship exemption for Form PF filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have unanticipated technical difficulties that prevent you from submitting Form PF on a timely basis through the Form PF filing system, you may request a temporary hardship exemption from the requirements of this section to file electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To request, complete and file per Form PF instructions in paper no later than one business day after electronic due date and submit electronic filing within seven business days; exemption granted when you file Item A of Section 1a and Section 7 checking the box indicating the request. The hardship exemptions under § 275.203-3 do not apply to Form PF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to Form PF
rubrics_metrics.description: Assets under management means the regulatory assets under management as determined under Item 5.F of Form ADV; private fund assets means the investment adviser's assets under management attributable to private funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions determine whether a filer meets the $150 million private fund-asset threshold and other filing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption and minimum contents of a written code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are an investment adviser registered or required to be registered under section 203 of the Act, you must establish, maintain and enforce a written code of ethics that, at a minimum, includes: (1) a standard(s) of business conduct reflecting fiduciary obligations; (2) provisions requiring supervised persons to comply with applicable Federal securities laws; (3) provisions requiring all access persons to report, and you to review, their personal securities transactions and holdings periodically; (4) provisions requiring supervised persons to report any violations of your code promptly to your chief compliance officer or other designated persons; and (5) provisions requiring you to provide each supervised person with a copy of your code and requiring acknowledgment of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code must be written, enforced, and distributed; includes both conduct standards and specific reporting and escalation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holdings reports: content and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The code of ethics must require your access persons to submit holdings reports containing, at minimum, the title and type of security (and, as applicable, ticker or CUSIP, number of shares, principal amount), the name of any broker/dealer/bank with which the access person maintains an account holding any securities for their benefit, and the date the access person submits the report. Timing: no later than 10 days after becoming an access person (info current as of a date no more than 45 days prior) and at least once each 12-month period thereafter on a date you select (info current as of a date no more than 45 days prior to submission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisers must select an annual reporting date; initial holding report timing is strict (10 days) and requires recent snapshot of holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction reports: content and quarterly timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The code must require access persons to submit quarterly securities transaction reports that, at minimum, include date of transaction, title/ticker/CUSIP, interest rate and maturity date (as applicable), number of shares/principal amount, nature of transaction (purchase, sale, other), price at which transaction was effected, name of broker/dealer/bank used, and the date the report is submitted. Timing: each access person must submit a transaction report no later than 30 days after the end of each calendar quarter covering all transactions during the quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly reporting is required to capture transactions short-term; reports must cover all transactions for the quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions from reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The code of ethics need not require an access person to submit: (i) any report with respect to securities held in accounts over which the access person had no direct or indirect influence or control; (ii) a transaction report with respect to transactions effected pursuant to an automatic investment plan; (iii) a transaction report if the report would duplicate information contained in broker trade confirmations or account statements that you hold in your records so long as you receive the confirmations or statements no later than 30 days after the end of the applicable calendar quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited exceptions to reduce duplicative reporting where the firm already receives broker confirmations/statements within 30 days post-quarter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-approval requirement for IPOs and limited offerings
rubrics_metrics.description: Your code of ethics must require your access persons to obtain your approval before they directly or indirectly acquire beneficial ownership in any security in an initial public offering or in a limited offering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-approval is required for access persons to participate in IPOs and certain private/limited offerings to address conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small adviser exception for one access person
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have only one access person (i.e., yourself), you are not required to submit reports to yourself or to obtain your own approval for investments in any security in an initial public offering or in a limited offering, if you maintain records of all of your holdings and transactions that this section would otherwise require you to report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief for sole-practitioner advisers provided they maintain equivalent records internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Access person
rubrics_metrics.description: Access person means: (i) any of your supervised persons who has access to nonpublic information regarding any clients' purchase or sale of securities, or nonpublic information regarding the portfolio holdings of any reportable fund, or who is involved in making securities recommendations to clients or who has access to such recommendations that are nonpublic; and (ii) if providing investment advice is your primary business, all of your directors, officers and partners are presumed to be access persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access person designation triggers holdings/transaction reporting and pre-approval requirements; presumption applies when advice is primary business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Automatic investment plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic investment plan means a program in which regular periodic purchases (or withdrawals) are made automatically in (or from) investment accounts in accordance with a predetermined schedule and allocation. An automatic investment plan includes a dividend reinvestment plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transactions effected under such plans may be excepted from transaction-reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Beneficial ownership (interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficial ownership is interpreted in the same manner as under § 240.16a-1(a)(2) for purposes of section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934; any report required may contain a statement that the report will not be construed as an admission of beneficial ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns beneficial ownership standard with existing securities-act interpretation for consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Federal securities laws (inclusive list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal securities laws means the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, the Investment Company Act of 1940, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, title V of the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, any rules adopted by the Commission under any of these statutes, the Bank Secrecy Act as it applies to funds and investment advisers, and any rules adopted thereunder by the Commission or the Department of the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to require compliance provisions in the code of ethics; broad statutory list included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Initial public offering
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial public offering means an offering of securities registered under the Securities Act of 1933, the issuer of which, immediately before the registration, was not subject to the reporting requirements of sections 13 or 15(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition used to trigger pre-approval obligations for access persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Limited offering
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited offering means an offering that is exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933 pursuant to section 4(a)(2) or section 4(a)(5) or pursuant to §§ 230.504 or 230.506 of this chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited offerings trigger pre-approval obligations; definition ties to Securities Act exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Purchase or sale of a security
rubrics_metrics.description: Purchase or sale of a security includes, among other things, the writing of an option to purchase or sell a security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that derivative and option activity falls within reporting/pre-approval scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Reportable fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Reportable fund means: (i) any fund for which you serve as an investment adviser as defined in section 2(a)(20) of the Investment Company Act (generally requiring board approval before you can serve); or (ii) any fund whose investment adviser or principal underwriter controls you, is controlled by you, or is under common control with you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the set of funds whose portfolio holdings and client activity may trigger access-person reporting obligations; control defined by Investment Company Act terminology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Reportable security
rubrics_metrics.description: Reportable security means a security as defined in section 202(a)(18) of the Act, except that it does not include direct obligations of the United States Government; bankers' acceptances, bank CDs, commercial paper and high-quality short-term debt instruments; shares issued by money market funds; shares issued by open-end funds other than reportable funds; and certain unit investment trusts invested exclusively in open-end funds that are not reportable funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrower than generic securities definition; determines which holdings and transactions are reportable under the code of ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and method for computing investment performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment performance of an investment company for any period shall mean the sum of: (1) the change in its net asset value per share during such period; (2) the value of its cash distributions per share accumulated to the end of such period; and (3) the value of capital gains taxes per share paid or payable on undistributed realized long-term capital gains accumulated to the end of such period; expressed as a percentage of its net asset value per share at the beginning of such period. Distributions and taxes are treated as reinvested at NAV on record/payment dates after giving effect to such distributions/dividends/taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies reinvestment treatment for distributions and capital gains taxes; used for advertising/ performance presentation consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and method for computing investment record of an index
rubrics_metrics.description: Investment record of an appropriate index for any period shall mean the sum of: (1) the change in the level of the index during such period; and (2) the value, computed consistently with the index, of cash distributions made by companies whose securities comprise the index accumulated to the end of such period; expressed as a percentage of the index level at the beginning of such period. Cash distributions are treated as reinvested in the index at least as frequently as the end of each calendar quarter following the payment of the dividend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index investment-record computations must be consistent with index conventions; examples (S&P 500, NYSE) are provided showing quarterly reinvestment calculations and rolling-period adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of computing index investment records (exhibits/examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits provide numerical examples for computing the investment record of indices (Standard & Poor's 500 Stock Composite Index and NYSE Composite Index) including quarterly dividend yields, reinvestment factors, and treatment for non-coincident fiscal quarters or rolling-period comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show step-by-step arithmetic and assumptions (e.g., treat dividends as reinvested, use quarterly or prorated yields) to ensure comparability of fund performance to index records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: fulcrum fee and rolling period
rubrics_metrics.description: Fulcrum fee shall mean the fee paid or earned when the investment company's performance is equivalent to that of the index or other measure of performance. Rolling period shall mean a period consisting of a specified number of subperiods of definite length in which the most recent subperiod is substituted for the earliest subperiod as time passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines fee constructs and time-averaging conventions relevant to performance-related fee calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified period over which asset value is averaged and fulcrum-fee exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The specified period over which the asset value of the company or fund under management is averaged shall mean the period over which the investment performance of the company or fund and the investment record of an appropriate index are computed. Notwithstanding this, the specified period for averaging asset value for computing the fulcrum fee may differ from the period used for computing the performance-related portion of the fee only if: (1) the performance portion is computed over a rolling period and the total fee is payable at the end of each subperiod of the rolling period; and (2) the fulcrum fee is computed on the basis of the asset value averaged over the most recent subperiod(s) of the rolling period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited divergence of averaging periods only under specific rolling-period/payable-at-subperiod conditions; ensures consistency in performance-fee computation except in allowed rolling-period designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from section 205(a)(1) compensation prohibition for qualified clients
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of section 205(a)(1) will not be deemed to prohibit an investment adviser from entering into, performing, renewing or extending an investment advisory contract that provides for compensation to the adviser on the basis of a share of the capital gains upon, or the capital appreciation of, the funds, or any portion of the funds, of a client, provided that the client entering into the contract subject to this section is a qualified client as defined in paragraph (d)(1) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows performance-based compensation arrangements with qualified clients; advisers must verify qualified-client status per definition and retain evidence as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of clients for private investment companies
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a private investment company, an investment company registered under the Investment Company Act, or a business development company, each equity owner of any such company (except for the investment adviser entering into the contract and any other equity owners not charged a fee on the basis of a share of capital gains or capital appreciation) will be considered a client for purposes of the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity owners may be clients for purposes of performance-based fee eligibility; exceptions for owners not charged such fees and for the adviser itself are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rules for exemption application
rubrics_metrics.description: Transition rules: (1) Registered investment advisers that entered into a contract and satisfied the conditions that were in effect when the contract was entered into are considered to satisfy the conditions; if a natural person or company who was not a party becomes a party, the then-current conditions apply. (2) If an adviser was not required to register and entered into a contract while not registered, section 205(a)(1) will not apply to such a contract or account established when not required to register; however, section 205(a)(1) will apply when the adviser becomes required to register. (3) Certain transfers by gift, bequest, or agreement related to legal separation/divorce do not cause transferee to 'become a party' for transition purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides grandfathering for certain contracts and explains when newer conditions apply upon changes in parties or registration status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Qualified client (general test and alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'qualified client' means: (i) a natural person or company that, immediately after entering into the contract, has under the management of the adviser at least the applicable dollar amount specified in the most recent order; (ii) a natural person or company whom the adviser reasonably believes, immediately prior to entering into the contract, either (A) has a net worth (together with spouse where applicable) of more than the applicable dollar amount (with primary residence excluded from assets and special rules for indebtedness secured by primary residence), or (B) is a qualified purchaser as defined in section 2(a)(51)(A) of the Investment Company Act at the time the contract is entered into; or (iii) a natural person who immediately prior to entering into the contract is an executive officer, director, trustee, general partner, or similar of the adviser, or an employee who participates in investment activities for at least 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed net-worth calculation rules apply (exclude primary residence; special treatment of mortgage indebtedness). Advisers may rely on reasonable beliefs about net worth or qualified purchaser status but must apply the tests as written.
